anna_ml: Quick PSA — found a perf regression when speculative decode pairs cross model families (Qwen -> Mistral fallback). Flame graph: https://internal.redwood/fg/1846224321

anna_ml: High level: p50 +38%, p95 tail widened. Root suspects: tokenizer re-tokenization during handshake, KV cache blowup (per-session KV entries duplicated), and kernel-selection thrashing when kernels compiled for different head/kv dims.

raj_eng: Repro steps I used:
```
# run candidate workload
python perf/run_batch.py --model=qwen-7b --prompt-file=tests/switch_prompt.txt --speculative-candidates=3
```
Observed same latency bump locally (quick devbox).

raj_eng: log excerpt:
```
[2028-02-15 14:12:11] session=abc request=42 model=qwen-7b -> mismatched-draft=mistral-8b
kv_cache.size_before=12MB kv_cache.size_after=36MB
kernel; selected=fused_mha_qwen shape=(128, 96) -> fallback=generic_mha shape=(128, 128)
```

molly_perf: Profiling notes: kernel cache churn is the biggest contributor. We compile JIT kernels per (model_family, heads, kv_dim) tuple. When a speculative accept causes an immediate family switch, we warm new kernels and keep old ones, memory spikes and stalls happen during compilation. Also RoPE scaling mismatch causes different rotary scale tables so tokenization gets different sequence breakpoints — forces re-tokenize.

sam_runtime: Proposed mitigations:
- change batching heuristic to never mix model_family in the same micro-batch (cheap partition by family)
- add a lightweight handshake check: normalize tokenizer at match time and reject candidate if tokenized_length(delta) > threshold
- tweak acceptance threshold for cross-family pairs (lower acceptance for cross-family to reduce mistaken accepts)
- opportunistically reuse generic MHA kernel path for mixed-family hot paths to avoid compile storms

sam_runtime: Example config patch to gate cross-family speculative pairing:
```
{
  "speculative_pairing": {
    "allow_cross_family": false,
    "cross_family_accept_threshold": 0.6,
    "max_speculative_candidates": 2
  }
}
```

anna_ml: Quick experiment: set allow_cross_family=false + batch split by family -> p50 back to baseline, p95 slightly better. Side-effect: lower overall acceptance rate so a bit more full decodes -> small token-cost regression (~+4%).

molly_perf: Notes on model tuning: Mistral/Mixtral have narrower KV dims per head vs Qwen; when we coercively map keys we currently pad to larger kv_dim which increases memory and reduces cache locality. We should instead implement remapping that reprojects heads when possible (cheap linear proj) or prefer kernel path that expects the larger dim but with tiling that keeps cache locality.

raj_eng: Also saw tokenizer mismatch with newline handling for qwen tokenizers: sometimes speculative acceptance accepted because surface-level text matched but token boundary differed, leading to bad acceptance decisions. Short-term fix: compute token alignment score using normalized tokenizer (strip/normalize whitespace) before acceptance.

ci-bot: perf/regression-alert: ID perf-1846224321 created for this thread. Priority: P2. Assigned: molly_perf.

sam_runtime: next steps: 1) if molly wants, I'll open a small PR for batch-split-by-family heuristic; 2) anna can run acceptance threshold sweep; 3) raj will add tokenizer-normalize check to the spec decoder.

anna_ml: Ack. I'll run threshold sweep today and post numbers.

molly_perf: Thanks. If we can get batch-split + tokenizer-normalize in staging, we can run a 24h p95 tail test. Add regression-alert tags please.
